question: What is the Agent-to-Agent (A2A) protocol, and how does it differ from MCP?
idealAnswerCore: MCP standardizes how a host talks to tools/resources (model-to-context). A2A (and similar agent-network proposals) standardizes how autonomous agents discover, auth, and delegate to other agents as peers — complementary layers, not replacements.
idealAnswerFraming: 2026 interviews love this comparison. MCP is USB-C for tools; A2A is more like service-to-service for agents. Stay high-level on evolving specs.
idealAnswerKeyPoints: MCP: host client ↔ server tools/prompts/resources, now stateless HTTP/stdio
A2A: agent cards, task delegation, cross-vendor agent collaboration
A product may use MCP internally and A2A at the org boundary
Both need identity, least privilege, and untrusted-output handling
Do not implement two protocols for the same local database wrapper

question: How do you design a computer-use or browser agent that is actually operable in production?
idealAnswerCore: Constrain the environment (allowlisted domains, disposable VM/browser), observe via screenshots/DOM with a tight loop budget, require confirmation on purchases and auth walls, and eval on your own task set — demo GIFs are not a control plane.
idealAnswerFraming: There is already a 'browser agent' question in the bank; this is the production bar: sandbox, determinism, cost.
idealAnswerKeyPoints: Sandbox: no host filesystem, no SSO cookies from the user's bank
Prefer APIs/MCP tools over clicking when they exist
Bbox/DOM actions need retries; UIs change
Record traces for replay; they contain PII
Kill switch and domain allowlist

question: What is prefill/decode disaggregation (Splitwise, Mooncake-style), and when do you need it?
idealAnswerCore: Prefill is compute-heavy and decode is memory-bandwidth/KV-heavy; at scale you split them across GPU pools and ship KV caches over the datacenter network so neither pool is stranded — overkill until you are GPU-bound on mixed long-prompt chat.
idealAnswerFraming: Serving architecture 2025–2026. Mention KV transfer and tail latency.
idealAnswerKeyPoints: Prefill likes high FLOPs utilization; decode likes KV capacity and batching
Disaggregation adds network hop and failure modes for KV transfer
Helps long-context RAG (huge prefill) plus many short decodes
Not your first optimization — continuous batching and PagedAttention come first
Observe TTFT vs TPOT separately after the split
idealAnswerFollowups: How do you keep prefix cache useful across disaggregated pools?
What happens if KV transfer fails mid-request?

question: When do you deploy an SLM on-device or at the edge instead of calling a frontier API?
idealAnswerCore: Choose local/edge when privacy, offline, or per-token cost at huge QPS dominate, and the task fits a 1–8B quantized model (classification, autocomplete, rewrite); keep a cloud fallback for hard reasoning and tools that need the network.
idealAnswerFraming: llama.cpp/vLLM/MLX class discussion. Quality cliff is the point.
idealAnswerKeyPoints: INT4 GGUF on CPU/NPU can be 'good enough' for constrained tasks
You now own updates, evals, and jailbreak regressions
Battery, thermals, and RAM are your new SLOs
Distill from a teacher rather than expecting 7B = GPT-4
Hybrid router: local first, cloud on low confidence
idealAnswerFollowups: How do you ship weight updates safely to millions of devices?

question: What intellectual-property and training-data issues should a GenAI product engineer be ready to discuss?
idealAnswerCore: Know where your weights and RAG corpus come from, whether the provider trains on your prompts, how outputs might overlap copyrighted material, and that 'the model wrote it' is not a complete legal defense — engineering controls are licenses, filters, citation, and human review for publishable media.
idealAnswerFraming: Not legal advice. Show you will involve counsel and still own technical controls.
idealAnswerKeyPoints: Provider terms: training on customer data, retention, output ownership
RAG: you can still leak a licensed PDF to the wrong tenant
Image/code gen: style and copy-alike risk; keep provenance
EU GPAI-style training-data summaries and opt-outs may apply if you train
Product: attribution UX and takedown process
idealAnswerFollowups: How does RAG citation help — and fail — as an IP control?
What do you log if a rights holder sends a complaint?

question: How do you build a synthetic-data flywheel that does not collapse model diversity?
idealAnswerCore: Generate with a teacher, filter with verifiers and diversity clustering, mix in real traces, and periodically inject new human seeds — recursive self-training on unfiltered model output tends toward bland, self-agreeing text.
idealAnswerFraming: Model collapse is the buzzword; the fix is filtering and mixing.
idealAnswerKeyPoints: Verifier first: unit tests, schema, entailment, toxicity
Dedup and cluster so you do not 10× the same intent
Keep a real-data floor (even 10–20%)
Watch evals on out-of-template phrasing
Document lineage of every synthetic shard
idealAnswerFollowups: How is this different from distilling a reasoner?
What collapse looks like on a classification head vs a chat model?

question: How should you evaluate multimodal (VLM) features differently from text-only LLM apps?
idealAnswerCore: You need perception gold (OCR/table cells, UI states) plus grounded generation; a text judge that never sees the image will miss invented buttons and misread charts — use multimodal judges or extractors and include blurry/rotated real scans.
idealAnswerFraming: Extends the evals domain. Perception vs language errors.
idealAnswerKeyPoints: Separate: did it see the number vs did it explain it well
Bbox/page citations for documents
Adversarial: tiny font, dark mode screenshots, memes
Safety: unallowed visual content, PII on IDs
Cost: images dominate tokens; sample evals carefully
idealAnswerFollowups: How do you gold-label a 200-page scanned binder?
When is OCR+LLM better than a native VLM?

question: What product and infra choices differ for a streaming voice/video avatar versus a text chat box?
idealAnswerCore: Voice needs barge-in, endpointing, first-audio SLO, STT error recovery, and recording consent; video adds lip-sync and GPU for avatars — you cannot reuse a 60s HTTP chat timeout or a long reasoner as the default turn model.
idealAnswerFraming: Product + infra. Tie to the voice system-design question without duplicating the whole architecture.
idealAnswerKeyPoints: State machine for turns; LLM is not the VAD
Partial transcripts will be wrong; confirm critical slots
Store audio with the same DLP rules as text, usually stricter
Fallback to keypad/IVR when STT fails
Eval with real call recordings (consented), not only text transcripts
idealAnswerFollowups: How do you test barge-in in CI?
Should the LLM see the full audio or only text?

question: What is prefix caching (KV reuse) at the serving layer, and how is it different from application semantic cache?
idealAnswerCore: Serving-layer prefix cache reuses KV tensors for a shared prompt prefix across requests on the same model replica; semantic cache returns a previous completion for a similar user question. One saves prefill FLOPs; the other may skip the model entirely — they compose.
idealAnswerFraming: Internals + production. Automatic prefix cache vs Redis GPTCache.
idealAnswerKeyPoints: Requires identical token prefix on the same model/quant
Helps system prompts and shared RAG headers if packing is stable
Does not make answers tenant-safe by itself — still isolate requests
Semantic cache can be wrong; prefix cache is exact compute reuse
Disaggregated serving must attach KV to the decode replica

question: Tell me about a time you killed or narrowly scoped a GenAI feature. What signaled it was not ready?
idealAnswerCore: Use STAR: name the eval or incident (faithfulness, cost, safety, ACL), the decision to delay or cut scope, the communication with PM/legal, and the follow-up eval cases so it could not silently return.
idealAnswerFraming: They want judgment, not hero shipping. Concrete metrics beat 'we needed more time'.
idealAnswerKeyPoints: Situation: a specific metric or incident, not vibes
Task: protect users/brand while keeping a path to launch
Action: kill switch, HITL, or retrieval-only mode
Result: numbers and the golden cases you added
Avoid blaming 'the model' without a control you owned
idealAnswerFollowups: How did you convince a PM who wanted to ship the demo?
What would you do differently in the next launch review?
